changelog: - **The two stage-derived company orders are bounded** (#2528, follow-up of #2524). `GET /api/companies?sort=movement|waiting` used to read every scoped company (with `needs` and the correlated `_count`) and every `StatusChange` row of every relation of those companies, just to slice one page out. It now reads only the scoped relations that have ever really moved (`statusChanges: { some: REAL_STAGE_MOVE }`, three narrow columns), their newest real move as one `StatusChange.groupBy` `MAX(createdAt)` row each — not a nested `take: 1`, which Prisma 5 paginates in the engine across many parents — and the `id`/`name` of the accounts that got a key. Only those are ranked in memory; the keyless tail, last by definition, is paged by the database in name order (`name`, then `id`, so tied names cannot repeat or vanish across pages — the plain `name` sort gets the same tie-break), and full rows are loaded for the page alone. The ordering rule stays in `src/lib/companySort.ts`: `rankByDerivedKey` (the existing `compareSortKeys`, then name, then id) and the pure page arithmetic `derivedPageWindow`, unit-tested in `scripts/test/company-sort.test.mjs` against the old rank-everything result for every page size; `e2e/companies-list-workflow.spec.ts` plants a newer no-op row so the aggregate's no-op filter (#2264) cannot be dropped silently. "Has this record moved" is still `lastStageMoveAt`, fed the single newest real row. One visible nuance: the never-moved tail is now in the database's collation order, i.e. exactly the `name` sort's order.
